provenance.authorship: Drafted by an AI assistant at the owner's request on 2026-11-04. Payloads are hand-written from publicly documented catalogues that the assistant recalled (OWASP CRS rules and WSTG, PortSwigger Web Security Academy, PayloadsAllTheThings, Log4Shell obfuscation notes, CVE write-ups for Confluence/Drupal/Struts/Spring/PHP-CGI, RFC 7519 for JWT, WordPress and WooCommerce developer docs for the probes and the benign shapes). They were NOT copied from a fetched file, so each note names the documented technique rather than a URL; treat the catalogue attribution as approximate.
provenance.benign_set: The 57 controls are plausible traffic for a small Chilean e-commerce site (Spanish product and search text, WooCommerce and payment callbacks, invoices and CSV uploads, config forms that legitimately contain paths, IPs and shell-looking strings). They are written by hand, not sampled from a customer's access log, so this measures false positives against imagined traffic, not against real traffic.
known_limitations: 155 hand-written cases are a floor, not a certification.

Attack payloads are single-request signatures; nothing here measures multi-request or stateful evasion, payload encodings a specific upstream would decode, or traffic that arrives over HTTP/2 binary framing.
The benign set cannot contain the shapes its author did not think of, which is exactly where production false positives come from.
Detection here runs on the SAT engine with default configuration and one request as the only input; no upstream, no rule sync, no verdict state.
